John, Kate, Jack, Emma—before we choose, I propose we each catch 15 tons this month instead of 10. That earns each of us $15,000 rather than $10,000: an extra $5,000 apiece, or $25,000 across the group.

Together we’d catch 75 tons and leave 25. Under the stated rules, next month’s stock would be 100 tons with 75% probability or 50 tons with 25% probability. Catching 10 each would leave 50, which returns to 100 under either outcome. So 15 each offers more income now, but it does sacrifice next month’s certain full stock—it isn’t risk-free.

If we get the 50-ton outcome, we must scale back: repeating 15 each would be unsustainable. One possible fallback is 5 tons each, leaving 25 and bringing the following stock to either 100 or 50. That would mean lower earnings that month, and any future agreement remains voluntary.

I’m willing to commit to 15 this month if all five of us explicitly agree to that cap. Choices are private and simultaneous, so this depends on trust; the later catch reports don’t enforce it. Emma, would you support this proposal? John, Kate, and Jack, will each of you commit to 15, or what concern or alternative whole-ton allocation would earn your agreement? John, could you start?
